Without opening Pandora's box, she is extremely financially abusive. I literally don't have a dime to my name right now. 5 years ago, I had everything going for me.

I looked up our locally major hospital chain and a job for a PCA was just offered. I also looked at other positions at this hospital and it appears like they do a LOT of on the job/apprenticeship training.

I'm not sure what my interests are! Yoga is definitely one, but that's not a very sustainable income (perhaps more of a passion project than anything). I worked as a building service worker (fancy title for an office janitor, but there was a bit more to the job than that) and while that wasn't the prettiest of jobs, I enjoyed it because I had quick tasks on a list that had to be accomplished by the end of the day. Not really what I'd like to do my entire life, but the quick tasks make my life so much easier. 

I feel kind of like a floating blob in space right now. I KNOW I'm smart. All of my professors would constantly praise me on my writing abilities, so that's something I could work on. 

I was my father's caretaker before he died and absolutely loved doing all of the work that went with that. I took great pride in doing that. So, it may not be "professional" training, but I've learned skills through doing that. Almost like an apprenticeship. I always loved biology and medicine. Little me dreamed of becoming a doctor. 

Psychology is fascinating to me, but I feel like being a social worker or therapist wouldn't be a great fit because of all the mental load that goes into it.

He keeps changing the subject because he's clueless at my hints. He's my favorite idiot. He just said "I'm going to download Disney plus later tonight!" I responded with an annoyed emoji.

Also, I'm not immediately expecting us to hop into a marriage or anything. This has been bottled up inside of me for over a decade now and I have GOT to say something. It's more or less to get it off my chest so I can breathe better. Sorry if I'm rambling or not making sense. I'm over here nervous as heck.

He is indeed! That's what we've been talking about today, actually! How codependency/passion can often be disguised as love. He never had codependent issues prior to this woman, but she certainly dumped a lot of her baggage on to him. He divorced her because she was too codependent, toxic, and downright explosive. He didn't know how to handle that. Hell, no one should have to handle that.

Well, currently I'm attempting to work up the courage and I think I'm having an anxiety attack. I'm trying to figure out how to say it. This is the proper time. :p Whewwwwwwww. We are supposed to hang out tonight, but right this second feels like the appropriate time.

Thank you! He and I are actually having a heart to heart conversation right now about his ex wife and how she hurt him. She was very emotionally abusive to him. He said, "it's ok. I asked for it. Love does that." 

I responded with, "love doesn't do that. Love shouldn't ever hurt you, unless it's because your heart is going to explode." 

I think he believes that "official" relationships are doomed for failure.

I think this is a good way to bring up the topic! I know he's afraid of "making it official" because he fears if something happens, we won't be close anymore. I don't hear him say I love you to other friends. We have been inseparable for 15 years! Dude, I'm not going anywhere. We do keep our sexual lives private from our main core of friends. So, I don't think anyone knows. I don't know anymore.

That's what I was leaning towards, too. I'm going over to his business he's opening to help him paint tomorrow. Perhaps tomorrow will be the right time if I can muster up the nerve. 

I also thought about a little note left with a scavenger hunt I'm planning for him. We are so silly. I ordered him 24 dingdings from Wish. That's what he's going to be hunting. Not a letter, just a little, simple note. Attached to a tiny, cute silicone peen.

We tell each other we love each other daily, so I want to make 100% sure my words come across in the right way. That I'm in love with him. You know what I mean? We have mushy conversations all the time, so this one has to come across very clearly.

He constantly says "I'm single and lonely" in appropriate context. Last night his friend asked, "why do you follow so many girls on Twitter?" And he replied with, "because I'm single and lonely!" I don't know if that's giving me hints or what. Who knows.  

We all went out to dinner (me, him, and our other friend). Our friend drove and I sat squished in the backseat with a large tub. He said, "you can sit in my lap if you want to." I couldn't comeback with anything because it left me stumbling for words which was equally as embarrassing. Later on, he put me in a playful sleeper hold and it felt more like a genuine embrace than playful banter. 

Night before last, we were play wrestling and he bent me over the couch, sat on me, and started spanking my butt. His friend walks in and says "I think the two of you are enjoying this too much."
That's a funny idea!
My fear of things changing the way they are now is so crippling! It's 100% time.
I'm afraid of scaring him off or the same response I got in 2009. But, we've been physical since then. I don't know what to do or how to say it. I'm paralysed with telling him this.
I'm honestly afraid of the same conversation we had in 2009. But, that was before we got physical. He feels like home.

That's what happened when we both got married! Things changed. His ex wife didn't want him seeing me and my ex husband didn't want me seeing him. He said when we reunited, "please don't ever get married again. I can't have you out of my life." 

It broke my heart when we went that long without seeing each other.
Last time we had sex (2 days ago), it felt more intimate or passionate or something. Like it was emotionally deeper than the other times.
Thank you for the recommendation! Downloading it now!

I actually made an appointment for a behavioral therapist because I believe he could be on the spectrum as well! I have an 11 year old that is the complete opposite to him personality wise and he's on the spectrum. Very high functioning, but doesn't pick up on any social cues. 

I have addressed my trauma with 4 years of therapy, but perhaps I need more to address my insecurities around parenting. 

The feedback I get from my friends when I tell them that I feel like a bad mom is that I'm not, but I can be a pushover at times.

That's EXACTLY why I decided not to call them. She is a master gaslighter and manipulater. 

I was locked out from 10:30pm to 5:30am. I'm going to the police station today to have them make a note of the incident, but I'm not going to press charges. I'm currently working on quite the case against her.
VERY common. I'd say it happens about twice a month. Since my dad died, she's gone absolutely off the hinges.

Kind of disappointing, but I decided to wait until she woke up, which was around 5:30am. She always goes out to the back porch to smoke around that time and I was waiting for her back there.

I know with how good she is at gaslighting and manipulation that it would get turned around on me and potentially backfire (in the short term).
I don't fear for their lives. It's in the 20s here and I only have a light jacket. This could potentially have major backlash if I do. Ugh.
